"He was alright, but his moped was a write-off."

You made me laugh at a man's head coming off because the way you said it!
He had-- He had-- Oh, god! "There's a man, outside our house"
"He had a helmet on, but his head come off."

q: Karl was picked at school for a special job. What was it?
a: Serving biscuits to old people
f: Karl: "'Cos I'm into biscuits."
ex: Even when I was younger, do you know when I told you when I was picked at school to give old people biscuits?
‘cos you had nice hands wasn’t it?

q: Karl bought a cheap book about "the Governor" from a seconds shop. What was wrong with it?

ex: Is this the book that you nearly finished reading, but you realized all the pages were in the wrong order?
Steve almost spits out his tea

He bought a cheap book, at a seconds shop, started reading, loving it. Then he started reading about this bloke and he went from jail to school. And then he looked at the page numbers and they were all out of order.

a: You always have a knife

You make one from a sharp rock

Ok so ‘pop over, get knife’ where’s that come from? Get knife.
Oh you always have a knife, of course you do. Otherwise you’re a fool always have a knife. Okay.
Well come on. If you’re going into a jungle.

q: Darren Buckley's dad, a copper, gave Karl and Darren a talk about drugs. What had he found in the bedroom?
a: A Skittle
f: Karl: "You know, the little sweets with the 'S' on it." Ricky reckoned the dad was bluffing "like it was a slang word".
ex: Funny thing with him is, right, when I used to stay over at his house, and his dad was a copper, and um, uh, I remember his dad came down and said, "Right, I want to see you two." And we thought, God, what’s happened. And uh, got us round…
You know, the little sweets with the ‘S’ on it.
And he thought it were like drugs!

q: According to Karl, what eventually happened to the teacher who set the 300-swear-word essay?
a: He got kicked out for hitting a kid on the head with wood
f: Karl: "He got kicked out for hitting a kid on the head with a bit of wood." Steve: "It wasn't you, was it? That would explain a lot."
ex: Nah, did it 'eck. The teacher I mean, he disappeared. He got kicked out for hitting a kid on the head with a bit of wood.
It wasn't you, was it? That would explain a lot.

q: In one of Karl's 'little conspiracies', why did teachers on his estate set homework to draw a bird's-eye view of your house and everything in it?
a: To find stuff nicked from the school, like the telly and projector
x: To check which kids had a loft
To pick the house for a school trip
To report families to the council
f: Karl reckoned it was to track down the stolen "telly and the video... And the projector thing". His own drawing: "Got nothing from me."
ex: And like the teachers-- because I lived on this estate, right? Loads of stuff used to get nicked and go missing and what have you.
And their way-- No, like telly and the video and stuff like that. And the projector thing and all that. So the way they used to try and find it -my little conspiracy- as you know, I'm good at them.

What they used to do is set your homework and say, right, draw like a bird's eye view of your house, right? But draw everything you've got in your house as well. So if you've got - I don't know - if you've got anything in the loft, make…
Right, so people with kids would come in with overhead projectors.
Well, that was the idea, I think, behind it.

q: Karl went to Madeira with his girlfriend's parents, who'd never been abroad. What did he tell Ricky her dad was packing just before they left?
a: Margarine
f: Her dad had already asked the best way to pack tea bags ("Put 'em in a jar"). Then Karl's news: "Guess what he's doing now?... He's packing margarine."
ex: Y-you remember last week he was, uh, worried- they'd never been abroad and, uh, her dad was saying, "How d- was- was way- best way to, uh, pack tea bags?"

Karl's going, "You get them over there." And he's going, "We can put 'em in a jar." He goes, "Put 'em in a jar." I phoned him up in the week, uh, just before he went, I think Friday, I said uh, "Have a nice time." And uhh- Sunday, and he…
I went, "What?" He said, "He's packing margarine."

q: Ricky asked Karl who he'd give £5,000 to: an old woman whose cat would die without an operation, or a man wanting a sex-change operation. What was Karl's sneaky solution?
a: Get a lookalike cat, say it's had the op, and give the man the money
x: Split the five grand fifty-fifty between them both
Buy the woman a new kitten and keep the change
Spend it all on a second opinion for the cat
f: Karl said he'd still want a chat with the man first, "like a second opinion thing", and reckoned five grand on a cat "can only be for people who've got loads of money."
ex: Alright, I’ll tell ya what I’d do.
I’d find out what the cat looks like, get a replacement, right? Say she- say it’s had the op.
She’s loving it, thinking it’s happy again.

q: Karl was worried that nobody in the papers was talking about a TV programme he'd heard about. What was it about?
a: A spider that's a foot long and eats chicken
x: A snake that can open doors
A fish that walks on land
A crab the size of a bin lid
f: Ricky had to stand up "because I thought it was gonna explode!" Karl's worry was that it was a foot long, yet "no one's talking about it."
ex: But there's always something- I mean, when we went- were out the other night, Steve, right? There's a program on about, a spider that's a foot long and eats chicken. No one-
[In hysterics] I don't know where to start! What do you mean? What do you mean?
I just- I'm sorry. I had to stand up because I thought it was gonna explode! What do you mean there's a spider that's a foot long and each chicken?

q: Ricky noted that Karl isn't bothered about going bald, war or SARS. So when did Ricky say Karl gets stressed?
a: On a Saturday between one and three
x: When his mam rings during Countdown
On the tube at rush hour
f: Steve agreed: "To be fair, you are worse than all those things... SARS has got nothing on you when you're in a right mood."
ex: He's not bothered. He wouldn't be bothered.
But I think, for someone who doesn't care about going bald or war or SARS or anything, you don't half stressed on a Saturday between one and three.
To be fair, you are worse than all those things.
SARS has got nothing on you when you're in a right mood.

q: Ricky asked how Karl had made it to 30 without getting squashed or eating something deadly poisonous. What was Karl's reply?
a: "I told ya I used to choke a lot."
f: It started because Karl's headphones were too loud, and instead of turning them down he just grimaced.
ex: (Laughing) I'm lookin' at his face, his headphones are too loud. Instead of turning them down, he's just grimacing, going, "These are too loud."
(Laughing Slightly) I don't understand it! How have you lived this long?! How did you make it to 30 without getting squashed or eating something deadly-poisonous?
I told ya I used to choke a lot.

q: A Brit in Lanzarote always soiled himself when he went out drinking. What did Karl reckon caused it?
a: The ice in the drinks
f: Karl: people buy Evian on holiday but "they forget about the ice." Steve agreed the ice cubes are "Made from tap water."
ex: It’s the ice that does it.
I—Karl is right, I think, it is the ice.
People forget, you know, they say, “Oh, don’t, don’t drink the water when you’re on holiday,” and they don’t, they drink, you know, they buy Evian and stuff…
The ice cubes, you’re right, in a bar. Made from tap water.

q: At school Karl had to write what he did every night in a little red diary. What did his teachers eventually tell him?
a: Just make something up and stop putting the same thing in
x: Write it in pen, not crayon
Stop drawing monkeys in the margins
f: Every entry was the same errand to Hugh Fay's for "a bag of potatoes"... "And a loaf." Steve's advice: "Start joyriding or something. Live!"
ex: So I used to put that in my diary every day and it got to a point when like even the teachers like just make something up.
Stop putting the same thing in.

q: Steve asked: if he and Ricky died in a tragic disaster, would Karl take Ricky's face or Steve's? What did Karl say?
a: Pop in again tomorrow and bring in another booklet
x: Steve's, as there's more of it to go round
Ricky's, but he'd keep his own ears
f: Karl: "It doesn't seem like any of them is like a great option." Ricky's dejected reply: "Oh, thanks."
ex: Can I ask this now? Let's say you - we were both - We passed away, sadly, in something terribly tragic. The nation's mourned, you know, it's just terrible! It's like one of the great national disasters. But, you.. at the same time, you…
I'm surprised you're asking this though, Steve..
I mean. I mean, it's just, it doesn't seem like.. any of them is like a great option.
And this is what I'm saying about the catalogue. If - if those two were on offer, I might go. D'you know what? Pop in again tomorrow. Bring in another booklet.

q: Ricky said Karl's completely spherical head made him look like a baby version of which character?
a: The Hamburgler
f: Ricky noticed it while Karl was sitting on Steve's knee having his picture taken: "It's slightly too small, I'm not being funny."
ex: I noticed the other day when Karl was sitting on your knee having his picture taken, it’s a long story, right? He’s got a completely spherical head. It’s slightly too small--I’m not being funny--’cause, I mean, you know, I’m not perfect...…
He looks like a little baby Hamburgler, and it’s sort of quite put upon, it’s...

q: Why did a bloke in the XFM office tell Karl his water filter was a waste of time?
a: It only works for a couple of jugs, then it's the same muck
x: London water is already filtered at the tap
It takes all the good minerals out too
The jug leaks plastic into the water
f: Steve and Ricky smelled a salesman: "Did he sell you another one, that he had on him?" Steve: "Yeah, a better updated model."
ex: ...em, water in London’s ropey. Em, an--an’ I use one of them water filters.

And the guy down in the office was sayin’ it’s a waste of time, though, ‘cause they only work for a couple of water--like, you fill your jug twice, and then the water’s going through the same muck, innit?
But it’s not--if it’s not getting through it’s not getting through.
If it’s a filter it doesn’t matter, does it?

q: Karl said he'd want Steve on an album cover. How would he improve Steve's image?
a: Put him in the distance so he doesn't look as tall
x: Sit him down on a stool
Put a bag over his head
f: Karl insisted: "that's doing you a favour." A moment earlier, Steve had called Karl picking him over The Chemical Brothers "the first sensible thing you've said for a long time."
ex: If I had the choice, I think Steve would look better on a... album cover.
What would you do, would you change him at all, to--what would you do with his image?
I’d put him in the distance, so I think...
I can’t believe this is, this is happening.
No just so you don’t look as tall, that’s doing you a favour.

q: What was Karl's top tip for not getting mugged?
a: Act mental
f: In Piccadilly Gardens a man wanted Karl's trainers. Karl "got a bit livid" and the mugger looked at him like he'd "got a right one 'ere", then left him alone.
ex: No, when we, when we were in that pub that night, and we got talking about muggers an’ that, the tip is, em, what I tend to do, ‘cause I nearly got mugged once: act mental.
You what? You nearly got mugged once.
But I--but I tried this technique, of acting a bit mental.
Right, and how did you act mental?

Well, this guy wanted me trainers... an’ eh, I was in Picadilly Gardens in Manchester and it was quite late one night, an’ he come up, he said, eh, “I want them trainers”. I said, “You want ’em?”, I said, “I worked hard for these”. I said…

q: Watching a TV countdown on New Year's Eve, Karl saw a nudist. What annoyed him most?
a: The nudist had a white sofa
f: Karl: "he had a white sofa. If you were a nudist you'd get a darker one."
ex: Well it was, we did stay in, and I watched that thing, you know, Hundred Greatest Moments, which was annoying me. Do you see uh, there was a nudist on it? You know how I feel about them.
There was a man with two knobs on it, and a nudist who uh, just like wonders about the house..

But it said, when he visits people, they, I was thinking, who let's him visit? And go, well you.. but he must go there with trousers on and go, 'hello, lovely to see you, can I just pop all these off?', 'well not really, no'.
And I tell you what annoyed me the most, he had a white sofa. If you were a nudist you'd get a darker one.

Wrote a postcard to every McDonald in town

That's when you read the phone book?
Well, so see how many Macs were in Scotland and I've got to Macintosh. Yeah, and it was like, you know 42 Pages for

q: Karl said postcards annoy him. Apart from there never being anything interesting on them, what's his problem with them?
a: Even though it's sent to you, you're the last one to read it

They always arrive after the sender's home
The stamp costs more than the card

ex: What does annoy me, though. You-you were looking at ‘em the other day. You know, you were talking about the pictures on ‘em. Postcards.
You don’t like, you don’t like postcards?
And just-just because there’s never anything of any interest and the fact that, even though it’s been sent to you, you’re the last one to read it.

q: Karl had never heard of prescription sunglasses. What was his logic?
a: If your eyes aren't good, the sun shouldn't bother them
x: Squinting is free, so why pay for lenses

ex: You see, I-I never knew you had to do that with-with sunglasses. I didn’t think you had to have the--
Right. Yeah, when it’s bright outside, people who wear glasses don’t need to wear 'em.
So they-they’re-they’re-they’re looking cool, but bumping into stuff!
No, but if your eyes aren’t that good then the sun shouldn’t be bothering ‘em.
No, I always wondered about Roy Orbison. Why was he doing that?

q: Listener Vicky asked Karl what would happen if insects were bigger than us. Who was Karl worried about?
a: David Attenborough

ex: Yeah. Okay: "What would happen if insects were bigger than us?"
Vicky of "Miltow".. Milton? Milton Keynes, maybe? It ran out, so.. I don't think there is a place called "Miltow". It's from Vicky. What, Karl? What would happen if insects were big enough...
She's going into the possible winner file, there.

Would uh, would David Attenborough still like his job? Do you know what I mean? Would he start worrying? [inauduble] got a point, just because, you know, insects and that - he's always messing about with them, but would it be that keen…

q: What did Karl's Uncle Alf, the cobbler, sleep in?
a: A rubber dinghy
f: Alf just liked boats, and in a tight bedsit he figured he might as well use the dinghy rather than have it get in the way. Ricky: "He moved into a dinghysit."
ex: And he slept in like, a rubber dinghy. Right? But he was-
Whoa, you can't just let that slide. Why did he sleep in a rubber dinghy?
He just liked boats and stuff and sort of-
Yeah, I like boats, but they're better on the water. Beds are better to sleep on. Boats are better to sail on.
Well, he just, he just had it in there. It's a bedsit. It was really tight space.
Boatsit. He moved into a dinghysit.
He's got this dinghy. So he's thinking, well, rather than it get in the way, I might as well use it.

q: In a 'get to know Karl' Q&A for new listeners, why did Steve say they didn't need to ask any more questions after the very first one?
a: Karl wasn't sure if he'd be thirty this month or next

Karl said he'd rather not say on air
Karl asked to phone his mam to check
f: Karl: "I'll be thirty next month... This month. No next, wha- where are we?" Steve: "I don't think we need to ask any more questions."
ex: I'll be, uh, I'll be thirty next month.
This month. No next, wha- where are we?
Ricky and Steve burst into laughter
I don't think we need to ask any more questions.
I, I don't- I think we've done it.

q: Karl said the 'I'm a Celebrity' contestants should've researched snakes. According to Karl, what do you do if one comes towards you?
a: Kick sand in its eyes - it has no eyelids, so it can't blink
x: Shout at it - snakes hate loud noises
Stand still and pretend to be a tree
Offer it an egg as a distraction
f: Snakes are deaf too, Karl learned, "so as long as you're really quiet" they'll leave you alone. The sand works because "it can't blink and it leaves it a bit, like, annoyed."
ex: They'll probably leave you alone. And also they don't have eyelids.
Erm, so they were suggesting, if one's coming towards you, just, like, kick sand in its eyes.
Cause it can't blink and it leaves it a bit, like, annoyed.
And it wanders off. But they didn't do any research before they went.

q: According to Karl, what were Che Guevara's last words to the man about to shoot him?
a: "Go on. Shoot me. Be a man."
x: "At least let me finish me cigar."
f: Karl stressed Che "wasn't scared, he wasn't like cryin' or anythin'". A caller with a PhD on Che later said he'd never heard those last words before.
ex: They executed him. They shot him. And, his last words, before he died, right, he’s got the guys there with the guns, and he wasn’t scared, he wasn’t like cryin’ or anythin’, he said to the bloke with the gun, he said, Go on. Shoot me. Uh…

q: In Karl's octopus story from 'some science lab', what did the octopus do at night?
a: Crept out of its cage, got into the crabs' cage and ate them
x: Turned the lab lights back on
Opened the fridge and ate the scientists' lunch
Escaped down the plughole into the sea
f: Karl admitted "I don't know if it's true", but the octopus "had had its eye on the crabs".
ex: Uh, a story that I heard I don't know if it's true, but there was some science lab somewhere, where they had some octopus in it and they had some crabs.. And at night, the octopus was like getting a bit bored on it's own in the dark and…

They like the dark. And the octopus had had its eye on the crabs, and at night when it's dark I was getting out of its little cage, crawling along the floor, getting in the crab's cage, getting them out and eating them.

q: According to Karl, what did Joanna Lumley do when she went on a desert island?
a: Made slippers out of a bra
x: Made a hat out of a coconut
Made a raft out of her suitcase
Made a hammock out of her knickers
f: Karl's summary of her survival skills got a big laugh from Ricky and Steve.
ex: D'you know how like, Lenny Henry went to the jungle, right, and you've got uh, who else did it. Joanna Lumley did it.
Joanna Lumley went on a desert island.
Made slippers out of a bra.

q: According to Karl, why would it be worth a company taking on homeless people?
a: They never have a lie-in
x: They don't need a parking space
They'd never ask for a pay rise

q: Accused of never doing anyone a favour, what favour did Karl say he'd done for Ricky?
a: Shifted his telly
x: Picked him up from the airport
f: Ricky: "I gave him a television! I gave him a bed, he went 'I shifted yer bed!'" Steve chipped in: "I cashed that bloody cheque you wrote to me!"
ex: I do do favours. I shifted yer telly!
Oh, hold on! He shifted my telly! I gave him a television! I gave him a bed, he went "I shifted yer bed!" - No, I gave you a bed! That's how he accouches things!
I cashed that bloody cheque you wrote to me!

q: Ricky brought up Anne Frank as a famous diary keeper. How did Karl identify her?
a: The woman in the cupboard
f: Karl later admitted: "If she didn't do that I wouldn't know about her, seriously. That's all I know about her."
ex: He went, "I've never kept a diary. Keeping a diary will always get you into trouble", and I said like Anne Frank. What did you say Karl?

q: Washing up in his high-street flat, Karl could see into the neighbours' windows. What was everybody watching on the telly?
a: The film Volcano
f: Karl had beans on toast because his girlfriend was away. Watching his neighbours' lives, he compared the scene to the film 'Sliver'.
ex: Alright? Now, I was stood up. I live on, like, uh, on a high street, right? So I'm washing up, I’m looking out the window. First thing that had me attention is I can, I can look into other people’s flats, right?
And it was weird how all these different lives were going on and I was watching ‘em and everybody had the telly on and was watching “Volcano”, right, which was on last night.
And I thought, “Oh, that-that’s weird”, right? I could see ‘em all watching it and it was like a little Chinese lad who was dancing around in some underpants.

q: Karl reckoned that with feet instead of hands he could still cycle to work. What was the one snag?
a: He couldn't pull the brakes
f: No brakes "because they're little, short things." But Karl saw the upside: "you're running in half the time."
ex: And then I thought, but I could still cycle in.
Well, that’s the thing. I was--
You’d be, you’d be really fast!
Well, that’s what I was thinking. I thought I could still cycle cause I could balance, but then I thought the only thing is I couldn’t pull the brakes.

q: Karl 'tweaked' Pulp Fiction's restaurant hold-up scene to be about Suzanne's hair. Where did he move the scene to?

f: Karl: "'cept it's not a restaurant, changed that, it's a barber's." Ricky's review: "God."
ex: About when she got it cut, didn’t like it an’ that.
So it’s sort of about that. Uh, listen to it, there’ll be a question at the end, win some, good stuff. All right?
And this is the scene where they’re in the restaurant, d’y’know when they’re about to do the, the robbery –
‘cept it’s not a restaurant, changed that, it’s a barber’s.

q: What was Karl's complaint about cave paintings?
a: It was always a Yak
f: Ricky: "I love the fact that 30,000 years ago they're being criticized for being a bit literal."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Arts · 2009
ex: But they always did the same thing. It was always a Yak, wannit?
Yeah, but they drew what they saw, I mean yeah. I love the fact that 30,000 years ago they're being criticized for being a bit literal.
No, but surely if all you ever see when you step out of the cave is a Yak, do something different for the wall when you get in.
Why is it always a Yak on every wall?

q: Karl restarted the row with Suzanne while talking about parallel worlds. What did he tell her about the other version of her?
a: They definitely won't have a haircut like yours
x: She'd be the one doing the washing up
She'd actually listen to the show
f: Karl: "Well, they definitely won't have a haircut like yours." Ricky noted his "very short learning curve."
ex: She heard about that off a mate, and we sorted it out, and I didn’t have to buy her anything, I just sort of said, ‘Come on, you know what the show’s about and that, stop moaning.’ That was all right until about Thursday, when I was…
Well, he’s probably taking some time off. Probably having a week off.

But I was just talkin' about that, and she was sayin', ‘Naw, that doesn’t happen.’ And I sorta said, ‘Well, they definitely won’t have a haircut like yours.’ And that sort of started the, the argument again.

Yeah, it’s almost like you haven’t learnt your lesson. Also, it’s like you’re talking about it again on air, almost, in a way. So her mates can hear it again. Very short learning curve. You know what? Karl, if there was a, if I cut a hole…

q: When Steve moaned about the cost of getting into town, how did Karl say he'd sorted his own travel problem?
a: He moved in closer and walks everywhere
f: Karl: "I've moved in closer haven't I, I'm not moaning about it, I walk everywhere now... I moaned about it but then I sorted it out."
ex: Oh yeah, driving into the center of town? Congestion charge, are you paying that are you? A fiver?
What do you think of that Karl? Eh?
Oh yeah 'cause he's Mr. er, Flush, he's Mr. Lavish-with-his-cash.
No, I've moved in closer haven't I, I'm not moaning about it, I walk everywhere now.

q: Describing how relaxed Ibiza is about mopeds and helmets, what did Karl say he saw a farmer carrying in a basket?
a: A goat
f: Karl also noted nobody wears helmets there and "You might even get three people on a moped."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: But by the same time-- When I went to Ibiza, right? Now, there they have motorbikes. People flying around on them. People don't wear helmets. You might even get three people on a moped. I saw a farmer with a goat in a basket. They don't…

q: Karl said he was sick of health adverts on the telly and listed some. Which slogan did Steve say he'd never seen?
a: "Watch your kidneys!"
f: Karl's list: "Don't smoke! Wear a helmet! Slow down! Watch your kidneys!" Steve: "I haven't seen that one!" Karl wanted a leaflet saying "use your common sense!"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: Forget all-- I'm sick and tired of having adverts on the telly: "Don't smoke! Wear a helmet! Slow down! Watch your kidneys!
Look after your liver! No, I don't know why... why can't they just put a leaflet through, saying "Hello everyone, use your common sense!" That's all I'm asking

q: How did Karl plan to get back at a rich girl on a TV show who blew her dad's money on shopping?
a: Work in her shoe shop and offer boots her fat ankles wouldn't fit
x: Sell her a fake designer handbag
Write to her dad about her spending
Charge her double at the till
f: Karl: "She really annoyed me and I'm not a nasty person... But she brought it out of me." Steve: "I'm not sure you're qualified."
ex: And I really wanted to get a job in that shoe shop where she was going in and blowing her dad's money and she was calling up her dad, saying “Daddy, is it alright if I, you know, I'm just out shopping, I've just bought some shoes that have…
She really annoyed me and I'm not a nasty person.

q: Karl's emailed 'psychological test': a girl meets a dream man at her mum's funeral, loses him, then kills her sister. What was the supposed answer?
a: She hoped the mystery man would turn up at the funeral again
x: The sister had secretly married the dream man
The sister had binned the man's phone number
She thought the sister was the man in disguise
f: Karl said the test was used on killers: "If you answered this correctly, you think like a psychopath." Steve had guessed the sister stole money and slept with her husband.
ex: That she was hoping that the guy would appear at the funeral again.
He'd- he'd go to the funeral.
Right, that's not a proper psychological test.

q: According to Karl's diary, why was his mam and dad's parrot looking worried?
a: It had seen the budgie and the cat go in the space of three months
x: Karl's dad kept saying it was next
The vet had given it a funny look
It had stopped being able to talk
f: The cat had "lost one eye and then it got into another fight and lost another", and Karl's mam and dad couldn't afford to "have eyes put on it".
ex: "My dad took the cat to be put down today because it kept bumping into things since losing its sight. My mam said, she's not going to get another one. She said the parrot is looking worried as it's seen the budgie and the cat go in the…
Your mum said, the parrot's looking worried. What happened to the cat then?

It gets into a lot of fights. It lost one eye and then it got into another fight and lost another and it was just walking around bumping into stuff. I mean, the vet sort of said, oh, we can do stuff to keep it alive and all that, but it's…
No, you can't have eyes put on a cat anyway.
No, but he said, oh, we can do something here. We can have its eyes sorted out.
